Technique identifiers, names and tactic assignments are from the public ATT&CK Enterprise matrix; the summaries are written for this project rather than copied. See https://attack.mitre.org/

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping
techniques.description: Extracting account credentials from operating system stores such as LSASS memory, the SAM database or cached domain credentials.

techniques.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Using RDP with valid credentials to interact with a remote host as a logged-on user.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Making a file or command harder to read or detect by encoding, encrypting, packing or otherwise obscuring its contents.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.description: Making an artefact appear legitimate by manipulating its name, location, extension or metadata.

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Registering a Windows scheduled task so code runs at a chosen time, on a trigger, or after a reboot.

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating running processes to understand what software and defences are present on a host.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Running commands or scripts through an interpreter such as a shell, PowerShell or a scripting engine.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Using PowerShell to run commands, scripts or in-memory code on a Windows host.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Using cmd.exe to run commands, batch files or chained tooling on a Windows host.

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Clearing Windows event logs to remove the record of activity from the host.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Communicating with external infrastructure over HTTP or HTTPS so the traffic blends with ordinary web browsing.

techniques.name: Data Staged: Local Data Staging
techniques.description: Collecting data into one location on the host before moving it elsewhere.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Using legitimate credentials to gain or keep access, which makes the activity resemble normal use.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Gathering details about a host such as its version, hardware, domain membership and configuration.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Enumerating local or domain accounts and groups to find targets and understand privilege.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: Changing an existing account - its group membership, credentials or permissions - to keep or widen access.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Bringing files or tooling onto a host from an external system.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Attempting to obtain credentials by systematically guessing passwords, including spraying and stuffing.

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.description: Changing registry keys or values to alter configuration, hide data or disable protections.

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.description: Using externally reachable remote access services such as VPN or RDP to enter or return to an environment.

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.description: Creating a local account on a host so access survives the loss of the original credential.

techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Decoding or decrypting content on the host so that what was transferred does not resemble what is executed.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Mshta
techniques.description: Using mshta.exe to run script content, borrowing the trust of a signed Microsoft binary.

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: Using rundll32.exe to execute code from a library, borrowing the trust of a signed Microsoft binary.

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.description: Installing or altering a Windows service so code runs with high privilege and survives a reboot.

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Adding an entry to a run key or startup folder so a program launches at logon.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
techniques.description: Finding credentials left in configuration files, scripts or documents on a host or share.

techniques.name: Credentials from Password Stores
techniques.description: Reading credentials from stores such as browser password managers, credential vaults or keychains.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Stopping, reconfiguring or uninstalling security tooling so that activity is not detected or recorded.

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Delivering a malicious attachment to a targeted recipient so that opening it begins execution.
